questions.stem: In a constitutional monarchy, real executive power is exercised by

options.text: an elected Prime Minister and Cabinet
the highest court of the land

questions.explanation: The constitution reduces the monarch to a ceremonial head of state while the Prime Minister, who commands a majority in the legislature, takes the real decisions. Britain and Japan work in exactly this way.

distractorRationale.a: Personal rule by the monarch describes an absolute monarchy
distractorRationale.c: Courts interpret the law; they do not run the executive branch
distractorRationale.d: Rule by the armed forces would be a military regime, not a monarchy

questions.stem: A system of government in which political power is held by a small privileged group is called
questions.explanation: Oligarchy literally means rule by the few. Where that few claims to be the best born or best qualified it is called an aristocracy, and where the qualification is wealth it is called a plutocracy.

distractorRationale.b: Democracy places power with the people as a whole
distractorRationale.c: Federation describes how power is shared between levels of government, not how many people rule
distractorRationale.d: A plebiscite is a direct vote of the electorate on one question

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of military rule?

options.text: Law making by decree after the constitution has been suspended
Strict separation of executive and legislative powers
Regular multi-party elections at fixed intervals
Collective responsibility of ministers to an elected parliament

questions.explanation: A military regime dissolves the legislature and issues decrees or edicts instead of passing statutes, so the ruling council legislates and governs at the same time. Nigeria was governed this way from 1966 to 1979 and from 1983 to 1999.

distractorRationale.b: Military rule fuses powers in the ruling council rather than separating them
distractorRationale.c: Elections and parties are normally banned under military government
distractorRationale.d: Collective responsibility to parliament belongs to the cabinet system

questions.stem: Nigeria returned to civilian democratic rule, ending its longest continuous period of military government, on
questions.explanation: The Fourth Republic began on 29 May 1999 when General Abdulsalami Abubakar handed over to the elected President Olusegun Obasanjo, ending the military period that had started in December 1983.

distractorRationale.a: 1 October 1979 began the Second Republic, ending the earlier military spell that started in 1966
distractorRationale.c: 12 June 1993 was the date of the presidential election that was annulled, so military rule continued
distractorRationale.d: 1 October 1960 was independence, long before the first coup

questions.stem: A government in which religious leaders rule in the name of divine law is called
questions.explanation: In a theocracy political authority is claimed to come from God and is exercised by religious leaders or in accordance with religious law. Iran and Vatican City are the standard modern examples.

distractorRationale.a: A gerontocracy is rule by the elders of a community
distractorRationale.c: A plutocracy is rule by the wealthy
distractorRationale.d: An aristocracy is rule by a hereditary or supposedly best-qualified noble class

questions.stem: Military rule tended to weaken federalism in Nigeria mainly because

options.text: the military abolished the states entirely
the army's chain of command concentrated decision making at the centre
state governors were elected by their own people
the constitution gave residual powers to the states

questions.explanation: An army works by orders passing downwards, so military governors and administrators took instructions from the Head of State instead of exercising independent constitutional authority. Revenue and decision making drifted to the centre, leaving the states as administrative rather than co-ordinate units.

distractorRationale.a: The military created more states rather than abolishing them, moving from 12 in 1967 to 36 in 1996
distractorRationale.c: Under military rule governors were appointed, not elected, which is part of the reason for centralisation
distractorRationale.d: Residual powers do lie with the states, but that would strengthen rather than weaken federalism

questions.stem: Every monarchy is by definition undemocratic.
questions.explanation: False. An absolute monarchy is undemocratic, but a constitutional monarchy such as the United Kingdom or Japan combines a hereditary ceremonial head of state with an elected government answerable to the voters. The test is who exercises real power, not who wears the crown.

distractorRationale.a: This treats all monarchies as absolute and ignores the constitutional variety

questions.stem: Which feature best distinguishes a totalitarian state from an ordinary autocracy?

options.text: Power is held by one person rather than by many
The state seeks to control not only politics but also the economy, culture and private life
There is a written constitution setting out the organs of government
The head of state holds office for life

questions.explanation: Autocracies are content to monopolise political power. Totalitarian states go further and attempt to reshape every sphere of life through a single official ideology, a mass party, controlled media, youth organisations and state direction of the economy.

distractorRationale.a: Concentration of power in one person is common to both, so it cannot distinguish them
distractorRationale.c: Totalitarian states often keep a written constitution while ignoring it in practice
distractorRationale.d: Life tenure describes monarchy and some dictatorships alike, whatever their reach into society
